rows: Isolate the power switch feeding the MK-II Speedtronic, located inside the Speedtronic.
Remove the external terminal block on the Isolate cards.
Withdraw the ten cards and take them to the laboratory.
Supply the card with 125 V DC (+65 on pin 11, -65 on pin 10)
Test the first gate as follows:

Make a jumper between the + supply on pin 11 and the Input on pin 1; the expected result is that the lamp of this gate lights, which means the gate is sound. If the lamp does not light, this means one of two things: the lamp is burnt out and the gate is sound — in this case it is determined that the lamp is burnt out by measuring the voltage, 12 V, at the gate output on pin 5, which should be 12 V DC; if the voltage is 12 V DC, this means the gate is sound and the lamp is replaced; or the lamp is burnt out and the gate is not sound — this case is recognised by measuring the voltage at the gate output on pin (5); if there is no voltage, this means the gate is not sound, so the gate components are inspected, the faulty ones are replaced, and the test is repeated by measuring the voltage at the gate output, which should be 12 V DC; if the lamp still does not light, it is replaced, and the gate test is thus complete.
Repeat the previous steps on the remaining eight gates
Repeat steps 1–6 for each of the ten cards.
Reinstall the cards in their places.
Reconnect the power again.
Check that the unit is Ready by placing the start switch in any position (Crank or Fire or Auto); the Ready lamp lights, which assures us that all the unit circuits are ready for operation
Check that there are no alarms on the alarm panel
